text.p: Global media giant News Corp Ltd holds its annual meeting in Adelaide on Tuesday. In the last year the following events involving News Corp have occurred.

Oct 10 - News Corp chairman Rupert Murdoch says in a newspaper interview that News remains on track for a 20 percent profit incerease in 1996/97 and that he is confident of winning his legal battle against CNN's Ted Turner and fellow media giant Timer Warner Inc.

Oct 9 - News Corp files law suit in New York court to block proposed merger of Time Warner and Turner Broadcastings Systems Inc. News claims US$1.0 billion in puntitive damages for alleged violations of anti-trust laws. News says its planned Fox News 24-hour news network suffered when Time Warner reneged on a promise to carry the Fox News channel, a competitor to Turner's CNN.
Oct 7 - News Corp launches its long awaited 24-hour news channel, Fox News, to compete with CNN and MSNBC, a joint venture between Microsoft and NBC.

Oct 4 - Australia's Federal Court rules in favour of News Corp's appeal against an earlier court ruling banning its rebel Super League competition. The decision clears the way for News to start Super League in 1997, creating a crucial sports programming element for its pay television joint venture in Australia -- Foxtel.
News Corp's STAR TV forms Asian sports programming joint venture with ESPN, a unit of Walt Disney.
Oct 2 - CNN founder Ted Turner apologies to civil rights group for comparing Rupert Murdoch to Adolf Hitler.
Sept 23 - Rupert Murdoch's eldest son Lachlan Murdoch is appointed managing director of News Ltd, the Australian offshoot of News Corp.

Aug 22 - News Corp reports A$1.26 billion pre-abnormals net profit, down six percent on previous year and down on average analysts expectations of A$1.343 billion for the year to June 30, 1996. But News said a budgeted profit increase of 20 percent for the full 1996/97 year was fully attainable, given a fall in paper prices, strong U.S. TV revenues and the success of blockbuster alien movie Independence Day.

July 17 - News Corp agrees to buyout the remaining 80 percent of U.S. TV station owner New World Communications Group Inc for US$2.48 billion by exchanging 1.45 prefered News Corp shares for each one New World share.
June 12 - News Corp announces creation of JSkyB digital pay TV joint venture in Japan with publishing house Softbank, agrees to buy indirectly 21.4 percent of Asahi National Broadcasting Co.

March 6 - News Corp's 40 percent owned BSkyB to pay US$270 million for 25 percent stake in German pay TV operator Premiere. BSkyB says it would also form a stragetic alliance Bertelsmann, Canal Plus and Havas to look at digital pay TV opportunities in Europe.
Feb 9 - News Corp agrees to sell HarperCollins Educational Publieshing to Britain's Pearson Plc for US$580 million.
Jan 25 - News Corp and MCI Communications Inc they announce they expect to have a satellite television and informational service operating witin two years.

Nov 20, 1995 - News Corp, Mexico Grupo Televisa and Tele-Communications Inc and Brazil Organizacoes Globo said they would lauch a satellite TV service for Latin America and the Caribbean for early 1996.
Oct 31, 1995 - News Corp forms global sports programming alliance with Liberty Media Inc and Tele-Communications Inc.

Oct 10, 1995 - News Corp chairman Rupert Murdoch says at company's annual meeting that he saw newsprint prices up 10 percent in 1995/96, costing US$350 million. Murdoch also says STAR TV would lose as much as US$80 million in 1995/96, but claimed he still planned to expand the Asian satellite TV operation.
